about: Every INSSPG type 2 variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 107 variables INSSPG type 2 writes to CADs/INSSPG/insspg_type_2_equations_onshape.txt, in that order (types 1 and 2 share one class and differ in fw_s_used and the mass code); 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file, plus every config key the CAD does not use (the config has two blocks, both merged into the design parameters); 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks INSSPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/insspg_type_2.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth), with Ft = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x sun pitch radius), qe = 1 / sun-planet contact ratio, qk = curve fit in Ns; fw_s_calc = b
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule: fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material and the safety factors, so the optimiser has no freedom over it

cad_variables.name: fw_p
cad_variables.rule: b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth), with Ft = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x sun pitch radius), qe = 1 / sun-planet contact ratio, qk = curve fit in Ns; if b < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, b is raised to that value; fw_p = b
cad_variables.reason: planet face width from the tooth-stress rule, raised to hold its two bearings; the ring width is the same value

cad_variables.name: fw_s_used
cad_variables.formula: Rotor_height - 2 - sun_coupler_hub_thickness + loose_clearance_3DP + sec_carrier_thickness + fw_p + standard_clearance_1_5mm
cad_variables.reason: printed sun length, type 2: the rotor height less a hard-coded 2 mm and the sun hub, plus clearances and the planet width; the type-1 rule is different (it uses the rotor support bearing); kept hard-coded on purpose until the designer explains it (docs/designer_questions.md, Q2)

cad_variables.name: ringRadialWidthMM
cad_variables.reason: ring wall: read from the config (the gearbox's own value is only the fallback); also used by the gearbox class and the mass code

cad_variables.name: sun_support_OD
cad_variables.formula: sun_support_OD_max if sun_support_OD_max < carrier_PCD - (planet_shaft_dia + planet_shaft_step_offset * 2) - standard_clearance_1_5mm * sun_support_clearance_multiple else carrier_PCD - (planet_shaft_dia + planet_shaft_step_offset * 2) - standard_clearance_1_5mm * sun_support_clearance_multiple
cad_variables.reason: sun support outer diameter: the space inside the planet shafts less sun_support_clearance_multiple clearances, capped at sun_support_OD_max
